gates.reason: Inspected filesystem writes, path construction, subprocess dispatch, environment propagation, receipt validation, and Claude/Sidekick handling; commands use argument arrays, identifiers are validated, evidence files are bounded and checked, and no current injection, traversal, secret-egress, or web-boundary defect was verified.
A declared check that exits with an ordinary nonzero code is recorded as failed but does not make the arm ineligible, allowing failed verification evidence to produce a succeeded classification.

Inspected process execution and evidence ingestion: output capture has fixed byte limits, hashing is streamed where needed, receipts have size bounds, and subprocesses have explicit timeouts and process-group cleanup.

findings.title: Failed declared checks can produce an eligible succeeded classification
findings.what: checkResultFromEvidence marks every nonzero exit as status="failed", but the final classification only treats null and 127 exit codes as tooling failures. Consequently, a normal test/lint/build failure such as exit code 1 survives all branches and reaches status="succeeded", eligible=true, corrupting the release-gate result despite reproducible failed check evidence.
findings.fix: Before the success branch, detect any check result with status="failed" or exitCode !== 0 that is not already classified as timeout, truncation, or tooling failure, and emit status="failed", eligible=false with a genuine-check-failure error referencing its checkId; do not authorize a tooling retry for that outcome.
findings.acceptance: Using deterministic check evidence with exitCode=1, signal=null, timedOut=false, truncated=false, no spawnError or environmentErrors, and a quiescent process group produces a classification with status="failed" and eligible=false; equivalent evidence with exitCode=0 still permits status="succeeded" and eligible=true.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 2750-2757 explicitly label exit code 1 as failed, while lines 3637-3644 exclude it from toolingFailure and lines 3692-3699 unconditionally select the eligible success branch when no timeout or truncation exists.
